utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next witness is Sejdi Lami -- Sejdi Lama.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you spell your last name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I am Sada Lama, S-a-d-a L-a-m-a.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Lama, you were born on the 8th of August, 1950?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in mid-July 2000?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you also testified in the Milutinovic et al case on the 12th of September, 2006?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And before you came here you had an opportunity to review both your statement and you testimony?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And together do the statement and the transcript of testimony truly and accurately reflect what you would have said if you would give your testimony orally today before this Court?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, I would say the same things today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm referring to the statement. It's 65 ter number 2271 which I would seek to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00661, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And also to the transcript which has 65 ter number 5084.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00662, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will read out a summary of this witness's evidence. The witness is a male Kosovo Albanian Muslim from Vata village, municipality of Kacanik. During the conflict in 1999 there was no regular KLA presence in the village; however, about a week before the VJ attack some 20 KLA soldiers stayed in a house in the village. They left the place the day before the attack. The witness saw on 13th of April, 1999, four Pragas and six lorries transporting 100 soldiers from a VJ unit entering the village. The population learned that soldiers had also surrounded the villages of Slatina in the municipality of Kacanik. When shooting started from Pragas and hand-guns in the early morning, about 300 villagers left for the mountains. The witness and his family left also and hid in a gorge. Serb soldiers came who left in the afternoon when the shooting stopped. With others the witness found the bodies of four men who were unarmed and had been captured before. The bodies were brought to Vata. That day seven more bodies were brought to the village from different locations in the area. In the neighbourhood of Caka and Tifeku, most of the houses were burned. On 14 and 15 April the whole population of the village fled towards Macedonia. On the way to Macedonia they were stopped by VJ soldiers who demanded money. They paid 500 German marks. The witness returned on 17th of July, 1999, to Vata. His houses as well as other houses in the village were looted. One of the 11 bodies which were initially -- which was initially buried in the cemetery, Ramadan Xhokli, was reburied in the KLA cemetery because he had been an active KLA member. End of the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I would just have a few questions, and I wanted to show you your statement briefly. That's 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's P661.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: P661. Thank you, Your Honours. And in the English version I would need to have page 3, the third paragraph from the bottom; and in the Albanian version, please, page 8, the second paragraph from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I hope you can read that. I see you have your glasses with you. Just -- it has appeared in front of you on the left-hand side of the screen, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This -- the Albanian version should be page 8. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could read the second paragraph which is in front of you here on the screen. I hope you can read this. Are you able to read?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I can't make it out very well. Is it on the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can also read it to you if this is helpful. I appear not to have a hard copy here. Yeah, I will read it to you. You stated here on the 7th -- on the 13th of April, 1999, "at 5.00 in the morning four Pragas and six military lorries entered the village." What I wanted to ask you: What was the colour of these military lorries?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: The military lorries had the normal colour -- the dark colour. I don't know how to describe it to you. It is -- it was -- they were darker than the colour of the screen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's the second paragraph. I hope you can read now. And why did you conclude that these were military lorries?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Because we saw them when they got off the lorries, I mean the soldiers, and they came through the houses towards the mountain. We also saw the lorries when they went back without the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you describe what the soldiers were wearing?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms, brown and blue. There were also some other ones wearing dark brown and black uniforms, camouflage, just like the American army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I did not see them from close up. They were about 3 or 400 metres away. If we had been close up we would have been killed. We could only see them from afar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you read further here in this paragraph you later on talk that among these 100 soldiers there were certain persons wearing red and black bandannas. And you say: "And I believe they must have been paramilitaries." Could you tell me what you meant by this.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Paramilitaries are reserve army or police. They had ribbons on their heads, black and red, and they were Arkan's army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Apart from these ribbons red and black on their head, was there anything else which you noticed on these gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They had black or dark uniforms, different type -- different from those of the army, but they were not civilian clothes. The uniforms were some of them black, some of them camouflage, but these with the black uniforms and the ribbons were more dangerous. Whether they were soldiers or paramilitaries, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And why do you say they were more dangerous?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They were more dangerous because they shot at random, and they killed you on the spot. They did whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But have you seen these people you describe as paramilitary as engaging in such acts?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No, but that's what I believe. I did not ask them, I did not speak to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you see that the soldiers and these black paramilitary persons were going together or separate once they were getting off the six lorries?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They were together, together.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what did they do together?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They went towards the mountains looking for people. The four Pragas stayed at one place, and they were shooting. We were -- the Pragas were placed at big meadow, and they were shooting towards the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody operating these Pragas?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. I just could see them from afar. We were very scared, you must understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Do you believe that Albanian villagers were operating these Pragas on that day when they were firing?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No, the Serbs. The Serbs did all those things. The Albanians did not operate such equipment, they did not have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you a map. It's 65 ter number 615.08. And if you can find on this map, could you please encircle where the village of Vata, is where you were living and where also these Pragas were put and the 100 people arrived, the 100 soldiers as you mentioned. We can also enlarge it. You just need to tell us whether you wish to have it enlarged.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Could you enlarge it a little bit because I cannot read the smaller script.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can enlarge it further if you want. You need to tell us where we have to enlarge it. Where is Vata in relation to Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in relation to Kacanik where is Vata?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Vata is here, but I don't have a pen to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you give the witness a pen, please.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you encircle that, please, because it's not a full circle.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you on the right-hand side of that circle mark a number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You marked it on the left-hand side. Thank you. Can you now tell me where you found the four dead bodies later in the day, and I'm referring to Mahmut Caka, Hebib Lama, Rraman Lama, and Brahim Lama. Could you encircle the location where you found these four bodies.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: These four men were found here on a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You've marked a big red dot to the left of the number 1, for the record. Could you now on the left-hand side of that dot mark a number 2, please, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You've marked a number 2 below that dot, for the record.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, number 2. I can't write very well with this pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No problem. It's enough. Could you tell us, that day -- the next day you were leaving towards Macedonia you said. Which way did you take to go towards Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: On the 15th of April we followed the Sharri road towards Tetove. We went to Dragonac, Gllobocice, and Tetove. However, they did not allow us to go through so we went back. On the 12th of April we went back because the border was closed. On the 13th the offensive was launched. On the 14th of April we went back to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And which way did you take to go to Macedonia, which border did you cross?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Gllobocica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark, if you find it on the map, the location where you crossed the border.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I can't see it very well. My eyes are not that good, you know, I'm trying to find Gllobocica, Doganovic. Gllobocica is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you encircle Gllobocica, please.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And mark a number 3 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark another number 3, nobody can read this. Maybe below that circle or above that circle, that's maybe the best, above.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Here you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I seek to tender that map, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00663, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Neuner. Mr. Djurdjic, do you have cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Lama. My name is Veljko Djurdjic, a member of the Defence team of the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. I have with me Ms. O'Leary, also a member of our team. I have a few questions for you, and let me tell you at the outset you are the most honest and sincere witness I've heard so far. I have very few questions in fact for you, just a few clarifications. I'd like to start with a few images.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up D002-5955.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for these photographs, I read your statement and I understood you to be saying that Dubrava is a large village and that there is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat what there is within the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Dubrava is a big village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question was whether Vata is within Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, it is within Dubrave. They are adjacent to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And within Vata there is a hamlet Lama, hamlet Safa, and hamlet Tifek?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, the Lama, the Safa, and the Tifek neighbourhoods, they are small neighbourhoods, but the whole area is called Vata comprising these neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We call these hamlets. Mr. Lama, on this map we've just seen where you drew the location of Vata, Dubrava is marked as a different place. Is there a distance between Vata and Dubrava; and if so, what is the distance?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: There is no distance between them, they are adjacent to each other. There are some villages called Dubrava and Vata, but these are adjacent to each other. Some refer to them as Dubrave and some others as Vata.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lama, do you recognise the location on this image?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I cannot see very well without my glasses. I'll try and have a look at it with my glasses on. Yes, I do recognise this photograph. This is the house of Nebi Lami, or rather, the house of his son who was killed. This one, a little bit further up, is of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and further up are the houses in Tifek neighbourhood. There's a road, and that's why I can recognise these houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this is the Tifek hamlet; right?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, we can see the Tifek neighbourhood beyond these houses, but if you can enlarge it, that would be better. The houses in the foreground are the houses of the Lama family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, should we tender photographs one by one or tender them as a set?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How many do you have, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are more, there are several sets of photographs with at least three in each. This is one document within this set, and I have another, and a third.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will use one exhibit number for each of your sets or groups of photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Now I would like to have photograph number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, what can we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: On this photograph I can see very well the houses, and I can tell you the names of the persons they belong to. This house here is the house of Brahim Lami. This one here is the house of Rraman Lami. Next to it is a stable. He was killed, massacred. This is the house of Rraman's brother. This is my house. You can only see the roof of my house. This here is the house of a relative of mine --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... you can, the roof of the house. Can you encircle the house of your house.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] You can't see it very well from the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What you can see, encircle it. I note that the witness put a red dot above the roof. What is the name of this hamlet, Mr. Lama?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] This is the Lama hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next photograph, please, number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because this is how marked, it must be tendered separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to tender it now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00087, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, do you recognise this hill?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, I do, very well. It is called Kodra e Keqe. Here up is the road coming out from the asphalt road. The asphalt road is below here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that a hill between Lama and Vata hamlets, between Lama and the rest of Vata?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Between Lama and Vata there is a stream, but the ground is not flat. This is the highest hill between the Vata and -- the Vatas and the Lamas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next image, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, which part of the village is this, what can we see here?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: This is the same photograph as the one we saw previously. Here is the asphalt road, below here -- here is a part of the woods that has been cut off, and from this side here, this area is called Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: In your statement you say that trenches were dug. Is there any of these photographs where you could mark the location where the trenches were dug?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] It can't be seen here, there were no trenches here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And on which photograph could we possibly see the trenches?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: The first picture we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The first picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we bring that picture up again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] You can't see it very well, but it's in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you now, although you say it can't be seen very well, just to mark where roughly the place was.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] Here is my house, and they should be here on this hill that is kind of visible here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here, it was here --

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: At this line. There is a meadow here, and here there are trees. It's right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lama. Put an X where your house was and the number.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now above this upper line put number 2.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So 1 is your house, and 2 is where the trenches were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender the exhibit now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00088, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I now ask for the photograph 4 to be shown. That's 4, but are there any more images? Can we see 5. This is the same picture we've already seen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Yes, the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. It's the same. Next one, please. It's the same picture. Thank you. Since they are a repetition, there's no need for the witness to give any more comments. Again, I'd like to tender them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Images 3, 4, and 6 of this set have not been exhibited, so they'll become the one exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00089, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we now call up D002-5966.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, what do we see here?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I see my place here, where I live. Here -- down here is the asphalt road. Dubrava is on this side, Dubrava and Vata.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Witness motioning towards himself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vata and Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this again your home village from a different angle?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I recognise this, but it's another Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What's the name of this Mahala?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: It's called Dugovi and Neziraj. It's near the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And how far are these houses from yours?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Not more than half a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, what hamlet do we see here?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: It's the same place, Dugovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, what do we see now?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: This is called Neziraj. This here is the asphalt road leading to Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this upper Vata?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This image will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00090, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly ask you D002-5961.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, can you describe what you recognise here.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] On this photograph I can see very well; however, I'm not sure whether this one is Ilir Caka or Rraman Lami. They were killed, and they were buried in the cemetery. I knew them very well, and they were very close to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which cemetery is this?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: This is the civilian graveyard in the Lama village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that part of the martyrs' cemetery?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: In the left side are the civilian graves, and on the other side there are seven or eight graves of people who were killed during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see image number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, could you comment on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I can tell you the people by names whose graves these are. This is Rraman's; this is Brahim's; this is Ilir Caka's. These graves are only 200 metres far from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On this mast, is this the Albanian flag flying? Whose flag is it?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] It's the Albanian flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next photo, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, what do we see on the tombstones? Who do they belong to?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] It's Rraman's tombstone, Brahim's tombstone; this one here is Ilir's tombstone; and here this is Hebib's, it cannot be seen on the photograph. And three other graves do not have completed tombstones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any symbols on the tombstones; and if there are, could you please comment on them.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: What kind of symbols, you mean flags or something else? I don't understand what you mean by "symbols." All of them were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, everything that you can see and recognise apart from the photographs and the names.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Yes, this is Rraman, this is Ilir Caka, this is Brahim Lama -- well, I can hardly see it, but Rraman, I'm 100 per cent sure because I can recognise him on the stone. Hebib Lama down there. And there are three or four people down there, Caka, Jakup, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What else do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Well, I recognise the stones and the names of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do we see any symbols on the tombstones that are recognisable?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] I don't see any symbols. There are no symbols. This is Rraman here. There is a book here, it looks like a book, because he was a pupil, Ilir Caka. The monument is in the form of a book.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What I want to ask you is this: You can see to the left of this tombstone, next to the image, the face, there is something marked there, engraved. Do you recognise what that is or not?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: This is Rraman Lama, and you see the name and surname there. This is Rraman, his picture, and his name, surname, the date when he fell victim as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Lama, to the right of the face do you see something marked there, engraved there, from the level of the head down to where the torso starts?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Right here you mean? Where are you asking? [B/C/S interpretation] Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So next to the image of the person to the right you can see that there is something marked there, it's lighter than the background.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] This one here?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's what I mean, yes.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Well, I can't recognise it. It's just some light reflection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, these are again photographs of the persons that we've already seen. Can we move to the next photograph -- no. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, Your Honours, I would like to tender those photographs into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That set will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D00091, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lama. You can take off your glasses. We won't need you to look at the screen anymore. Mr. Lama, we are now talking about March 1999. Who did you live with in your household in March and April?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian Interpretation] I lived with my own children, my wife and my children in my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And any other relatives, parents, brothers, cousins, uncles, did you live together with them in a communal household, or did you live apart?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Not in my house, no. I was with my family, my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me, the houses in the village, were the yards walled off?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No, no. There are no walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And please tell me, how did they take the hunting rifle from you?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] They took the hunting rifle -- well, I forget now but it was two years before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what kind of a rifle was it, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember, it was actually 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: 1994, what kind of a rifle was it, do you know what make?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: It was a hunting rifle used for hunting, if you know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: It was R-12.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please speak into the microphone because the interpreters can't hear him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had all the papers for the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who gave you the documents?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What police?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: In Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In Kacanik. Thank you. Mr. Lama, I just want to check if the years listed here are correct. It says here that from 1975 until 1997, you lived in Germany; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did you make any contributions to Bujar Bukoshi's government?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lama, before March 1999 did you hear about the KLA at all or UCK?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how did you know that other villagers were not in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: In my village there were no members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. And why then those who dug the trenches, who were members of the KLA, why were they doing that?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They dug the trenches for defence purposes because they feared that there would be an attack, and they opened those trenches. The Serbs also had trenches and bunkers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, were those trenches used to defend the village?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that half of them were in uniform and half of them were in civilian clothes. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] Yes, because I saw them. They were close to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know, can you tell me in paragraph 10 of your statement you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in order for you to be able to follow, I marked each paragraph with a number. So when I say that it's in paragraph 10, it's in paragraph 10 of all of the versions of the statements, English, Albanian alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, in paragraph -- you say that one day before the 4th of April [as interpreted] an order came to -- for the KLA to leave the village. Who ordered that?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I did not see who gave the order, but we heard. There was word. They told us that we had to leave our village because the Serbs were coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when did the KLA leave the village, at what time, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They left on the 12th, early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, I'm not sure that we have the same statement. You have mentioned first a passage that says half of them were in civilian clothes and half in uniform. I can't find that anywhere. And then with your last lot of questions you said that something happened on the 4th of April, and I can't find that anywhere in the statement I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not mention the 4th of April, and let me tell you I may have made a mistake about this half and half military/civilian. I do apologise. What I said about half and half, what was confirmed, that's from Milosevic transcript, page 4401, lines 7 and 8, there were 20 of them, but half wore uniforms and half wore civilian clothes. I do apologise. It's in the Milosevic transcript. Let me just ask it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this what I read out correct, Mr. Lama?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think that we need to show the transcript now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, I may have made a mistake. So the day before, we're talking about the 13th of April, not the 4th of April, so the day before you say that they had left the village. Okay. In paragraph 11 you say that on the 23rd of March you went to Urosevac because you heard that Urosevac would be attacked. Who did you hear that from and who was supposed to actually attack it?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Ferizaj would be attacked by the Serb army, and we were told to go and get our family from Ferizaj. We took our tractors and drove back together with the family to the village because we heard, as I said, that the Serbs would attack. They were shooting all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And were there not Serb forces in Urosevac even before when you brought your family there?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Yes, there were Serb forces in Urosevac. [Albanian interpretation] Yes, there were Serb forces, but they didn't kill the people at that time. People left towards the mountains. However, they were beating them and doing every other evil thing to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 12 you say that NATO launched the air-strikes during the night. What do you know? What were the targets? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I saw at 8.00 p.m., I was on my balcony when they targeted Picrrak. NATO would bomb during the night, and the Serbs would shell us during the day. We were amongst two fires.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you headed to Macedonia a week before the 13th of April, did you go across the Sar a mountain towards Tetovo, towards Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: We climbed the mountain to cross at Luboten, but because the snow was very high and it was very cold, the children couldn't cope so we went back home. On the 14th of April we left again by car and tractors to Gllobocica by the main road. When we got there we were stopped. We had some small children, they were sick, and I told one of the soldiers, the Serbs, and I asked him, Can we leave the convoy, please, because the children are ill. That soldier asked for a thousand Deutschemarks, and I said, I don't have that money. And he then allowed us to go ahead. The army was going before us. We followed them, and then at a turn they allowed us to go by ourselves, but we had to give them money. I paid 500 Deutschemarks. There were three families with tractors that -- we were allowed to cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you about that occasion. One week before you headed across the mountain. You didn't take the road to get to Macedonia; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: A week earlier we tried to climb the mountain, but we went back to the village because we couldn't -- because of the snow, we couldn't go across. The offensive caught us in our houses, and then we went to the mountain to hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the others who didn't have small children went on across the mountain and actually reached Macedonia; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: The ones who did not have small children, I don't know. Whoever was able to walk, they crossed the mountains; the ones that were not able went back to the village. There were about 70 or 80 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 15 you mentioned a small forest called Picrak, if I read it correctly, and you say -- Picrak, okay. And now I would like to know how far this wooded area is away from the village of Baince.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: It's next to it. Picrrak is next to Baince. Not even 500 metres between them. Picrrak is a mountain, the Drzava mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how far was it from your village? I'm talking about Baince.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: You mean as the crow flies or by road? By road it's about 7 kilometres away. As the crow flies, I don't know, maybe 3 or 4 kilometres, not even that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 13th of April you say -- well, 1999, you say that you saw Pragas and soldiers. Where were you at 5.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: On the 13th of April we left home at about 5.00 in the morning. We went up to a hill. The Pragas were stationed on the field or meadow --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the story short. I want to know where you were at 5.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] I left the house at 5.00, and I headed towards the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it daylight at 5.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No not yet. It was still a bit dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now tell me, how far is Slatina from your village?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] It's not too far from us, 2 kilometres maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how far is your village from Brod?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Brodi is a little bit further, 6 kilometres away. I'm not very sure, but I'm calculating in my mind. It takes half an hour to walk there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that you had planned a shelter in the gorge in case of an attack and that you had brought some food there, but were there any plans to dig trenches around the village?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No. The whole village, the people of the village, went towards the stream to hide because the army were shelling and shooting. There was a plane flying over, observing. Later on during the night we would go back to our homes. During the day we went to the stream; at night we would be at home. We did not have any trenches or bunkers or things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 22 you say that when the soldiers entered the village we all went out of the houses and started walking towards the Ljuboten mountain. Can you please tell me yes or no, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: On the 13th of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm reading from your statement, and I'm just asking you whether this is correct or not. When the soldiers entered the village, we all went out of the houses and started walking towards the Ljuboten mountain.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Yes, we wanted to go and take shelter, but this was to be safe, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were not an eye-witness of the killing of the four people by the path up there by the gorge; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You were not an eye-witness of the death of the seven people from other hamlets; am I right again?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] Those seven that were killed, I know about them. But about those four that were killed, I saw them because I was about 200 metres away --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let's take this slowly. My question was: Am I right when I say that you were not an eye-witness of the death of the seven people. So did you see that? Were you an eye-witness of that incident or not? That's the only thing I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Those four, yes; the other seven, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you saw how they were killed?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I was together with my wife. My wife was in the meadow. I was down in the stream. I did not see them at the moment they were killed, but I saw them lying there. My wife told me about their killing, and I came out of that stream, and I said, Let them kill me as well. The army was still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree with me that all those 11 people were fit for military service?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Rraman was more than 50 years old. He was not able to serve the KLA. Brahim was a student, 18 or 19 years old. One of his legs was 10 centimetres shorter, so he was not an able-bodied man that could serve in the KLA. Brahim was also -- Hebib --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- was not also an able-bodied man. Nobody was able-bodied men --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you don't agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] No, they were not fit to serve in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lama, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much. This completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Is there re-examination, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have a very few questions, Your Honour, and maybe I could address them after the break. I would streamline everything. I think we're not talking about more than a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have, then, our first break. We must have a break now, and after the break Mr. Neuner will have a few questions for you. We will resume now at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness, again. You were asked by my learned colleague about the KLA leaving Vata, and you responded the KLA left on the 12th, early in the morning. I wanted to ask you in which month and which year was the KLA leaving on the 12th Vata?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: It was April, the fourth month of the year, the 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And which year, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how did you find out that the KLA was leaving that morning?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: When I woke up in the morning they were not there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Meaning at the trenches or ...

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Yes, they had left that place. I don't know where they went from there. I did not ask them. They did not tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then referring to the KLA trenches, I wanted to ask you when the Serb forces in lorries, the about 100 men, came to Vata on the 13th of April, were these trenches used to prevent them coming to the village?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No, they were not used to prevent the Serbs. The Serbs could not be prevented. The Serbs took their own positions, and we had nothing to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were the Serb forces who came to Vata on the 13th of April shot at from the Albanian side?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were referring to four persons, Mahmut Caka, Hebib Lami, Rraman Lami, and Brahim Lami, who you had found somewhere in the [indiscernible] dead on the 13th of April. Then you said to my learned colleague a moment ago that you had seen them alive some 200 metres away. Could you explain where was your position when you last saw them alive?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: We were at a meadow close to a stream. The women and the children were on the meadow, and they saw them when they were caught, and they marched them up and down the village three or four times, and then they killed Brahim, Hebib, and the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, see the four persons?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: After they were killed I went there and saw them after they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What time of the day was it when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: It was 6.30 or maybe 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when -- about what time did the women who were on the meadow see the men last alive?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: 6.00. We had left together with the women --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to know the time. Then you saw the bodies, and they were transported to Vata. Can you tell me what clothes were the bodies wearing?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Civilian clothes, normal clothes, track suit bottoms, jeans, shoes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think these questions were fit for direct examination. I gave no cause for these questions in my cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can respond because you questioned that -- or you put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, not "you." Address us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I wanted to put that the counsel has put to this witness that the four persons were KLA members, and I'm trying to establish their status as a possible combatant, Your Honours, by asking about the clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The questioning, Mr. Djurdjic, as far as it's gone appears to be in order because you have raised the question whether they may or may not have been combatants. Please carry on, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you see or find any weapons on the bodies of the four men which you transported with others to Vata?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They did not have anything at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No weapons you mean?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: They had absolutely no weapons on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then I'm asking about the seven other members who -- of the Albanian side who were later that day brought also to Vata and who were dead. Did you see any or find any weapons on them because you were also involved in the burial I understand?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What clothes were these seven men wearing?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Civilian clothes, simple, normal clothes, normal shoes, jeans.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did they wear any uniforms from the KLA or KLA insignia?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then I have a few questions relating to the issue of NATO air-strikes raised by my learned colleague. Can you tell me in April -- sorry, in March and April 1999, were there any NATO air-strikes launched on Vata itself?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were there any air-strikes launched on Dubrava itself in the [overlapping speakers]... time-period?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So when you left on the 13th -- or after the 13th of April, 1999, did you leave because you were afraid of NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I feared the Serbs, not NATO. NATO intervened to help us, not to exterminate us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned in your testimony that even a week before the 13th of April you tried to leave Vata towards Ljuboten mountain. On that occasion did you leave because of fear of NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: SADA LAMA
utterances.text: I only feared the Serbs. In April NATO was -- NATO did not start the air-strikes in April; they started on the 24th of March. And NATO only targeted the positions, the tanks, and the bunkers of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lama, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber has been assisted by your evidence and by your earlier statement that you've given. We would like to thank you very much for being prepared to come to The Hague again. You may now of course leave and go back to your normal affairs, and the court officer will assist you out. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Nilsen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The next witness is Mr. Isa Raka, who will testify pursuant to 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: When he is ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be obviously extremely convenient if this witness could be concluded today, if both counsel would keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please read aloud the affirmation which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Ms. Nilsen has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Raka.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Will you please state your full name and birth date for the record.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Isa Raka. I was born on the 17th of September, 1971.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecution in 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And did you in September 2006 provide additional information and give an amended version of your previous statement to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to read through these statements before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender the Rule 89(F) statement from the witness Isa Raka from 8th of September, 2006. That's 65 ter number 02301.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00664, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Raka, did you also testify on the 19th of September, 2006, in the Milutinovic et al. case?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to review the transcript together with a language assistant before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the information you gave then in 2006 is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief, and would you provide the same answers today?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, it is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And I would also like to seek, Your Honours, to tender 65 ter 05087 which is the transcript of the testimony in the Milutinovic et al. case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00665, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would also like to seek to tender the exhibits that were associated with Mr. Raka's testimony last time, which are two marked photographs. They were annotated by the witness in his previous testimony. I will present for the witness also unmarked versions of these photographs. But since he's testifying pursuant to Rule 92 bis, I would like to tender these associated exhibits as well. They are 65 ter number 05088 and 05089.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 05088 will be assigned P00666; and 65 ter number 05089 will be assigned P00667, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I would now like to read out the court summary for the witness, and after that I have just a few questions for the witness. The witness is a Kosovo Albanian Muslim from the town Kacanik. The witness describes that from the beginning of March 1999 there was an increase in police activity in his town. On the 27th of March, 1999, the witness observed two military jeeps and a white Lada Niva vehicle driving into the lime factory situated on the other side of the Lepence river from his house. About 20 to 30 police officers and two officers wearing VJ uniforms came out of the vehicles. The witness recognised the deputy police commander in Kacanik giving orders to the others. The witness observed the officers taking positions on the upper part of this factory, carrying automatic rifles and mortars. They started shooting towards the houses on the other side of the river and two guards of the factory were later found dead. A bullet hit the witness's pregnant wife, and this bullet went through her right hip. On the 28th of March, 1999, the witness and a large group of people started walking through the woods towards Macedonia. The witness was in a group of 13 and 14 people who helped carry his wounded wife on a stretcher. When they came to the Macedonian border it was blocked, and about 700 people had to stay in the woods for two days. The witness and his group managed to contact some locals who helped them eventually cross the border to Macedonia. The witness's wife was sent to hospital in Skopje, and the doctors removed the child which was already dead. The witness's wife subsequently died on the 5th of April, 1999, due to blood loss. This is the end of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, we know from your statement that around 10.00 on the 27th of March, 1999, you went to see your neighbour Jakup Jakupi whose house was located up to the hills from yours and that you had a view to the lime factory from this house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: How far would you say you approximately were standing observing these things happening outside the lime factory, from the window you were standing in to the factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Approximately 100 metres as the crow flies, more or less 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: These approximately 20 or 30 policemen that you saw parking outside the factory, what were they doing after they parked their vehicles? What did you observe they were doing exactly?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They got off their jeeps. The police, whom I recognised who was in the white Lada Niva, started to give them instructions to direct them to the places where they had to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And this person who gave instruction, did you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. From what I could observe he looked like Lubisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And that would be, according to your knowledge ...

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: He was a policeman. Later on I learned that he was the deputy commander of the police station in Kacanik. He lived in my neighbourhood in an apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And after you saw this person gave this -- deputy commander gave this order to the rest of the group, what did this group of officers and soldiers do?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They started to crawl around the factory. And when they reached the factory, they climbed the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did you see them taking up positions inside the factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Can you just describe briefly where you saw them taking up these positions.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They climbed the stairs and appeared on the windows of the factory building.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If you could go to 65 ter number 02310, I would like to zoom in on the first picture which is K022-3167 -- or 68 -- yeah, exactly, this is the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I would like you, Mr. Raka, to just describe what you see on this picture and from where is it taken.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: This photograph was taken from the position from where I was observing, more or less 1 or 2 metres' difference from the place from where I was observing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: From your neighbour's place you mean?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And then if you could go to the next picture which is K022-3167.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: This is the same lime factory from another angle; is that right, Mr. Raka?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Would you be able to show us where you saw these people park their cars and taking up positions in this picture?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They parked their vehicles somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, I've lost the connection with the picture. I would like you, Mr. Raka, just to put a cross where you mean they parked their vehicles, if you are able to mark that on the picture.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Here approximately. There were three jeeps parked around this area, but they occupied a larger area obviously.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you just mark with a bigger cross so it's easier for the Court to see.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And then I just would like you to mark where you observed the forces taking up positions inside the building.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The police positions were here, at these windows here. One of the jeeps went down to the factory and then returned, and then those men from that jeep took positions up here.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And can I just ask you, is this the highest building in the town as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I would like to tender this picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00668, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And could we then have the last picture of the same exhibit zoomed in which is K0223169, I believe. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And if you could please, Mr. Raka, just point out to us with a number 1 the house where you were staying and observing these things happened outside and inside the lime fabric, the house of your neighbour, that's number 1.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And then I would like you to put number 2 next to a house that you owned or that you lived together with your wife that's deceased.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. You provided to the Office of the Prosecution these pictures when you testified in 2006; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did you take them yourself?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately when you took this picture?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I think it was in 2002. 2002, sometime in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And the other pictures that we looked at that you took them from the house that you were staying, a neighbour house, but which position is this picture taken from?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: This was taken from the balcony of the factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that in the beginning of April your wife died at a hospital in Macedonia due to blood loss from the wound that she got when she was shot?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Then I have no further confession for the examination-in-chief. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nilsen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: We would also like to seek to tender this picture. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00669, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let this photograph remain on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Raka. I'm attorney Veljko Djurdjic, member of the Defence team of the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic; and with me is Marie O'Leary, a member of our team. I have a few questions for you. If something is unclear in my questions, please say so and I will try to rephrase. What struck me is that it says here that you gave the first statement between the 12th and the 26th of November, 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you gave your statement over a period of 14 days to a representative of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what is correct then?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I gave my first statement in 1999. Several days later they came again to make some amendments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As I read your statement I didn't understand whether you actually were employed at any point in your life.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I worked in 1990. I was employed for six months in a firm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when we're talking about the firm, this factory, is this the lime factory? What did this factory produce?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: It produced lime.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this a state-owned factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe it was at the time. I know that there were people working there before that time because during this period, for some time the employees did not go to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And there was security in the factory at that time, in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And your brother, did he work in the municipality in Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Gezim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there other Albanians working in the municipality of Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know. He worked as a guard there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the 27th of March, in the afternoon, did you hear that the police station in Kacanik was attacked?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know where the village of Bob is located?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Based on this photograph, it's on the other side of the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I see the photographs. Are you referring to the photographs 022368?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... 23168.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, is it behind the hill, that village, or can we see it on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please explain "yes." So can we see the village, or is it behind the hill so we can't see it? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The houses right behind the factory are the houses of Bob village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you had a very good view of the village of Bob. Well, were you able to see or hear any gun-fire in the village of Bob on the 27th of March in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, there wasn't any gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And from that hill to your house, how far is it?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: As the crow flies or by road?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Two-hundred metres possibly, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I had information that around 1800 hours on the 27th of March an attack was launched from the factory on a military column that was in the village of Bob. Well, did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have this photograph 223618 in front of us, and having read your statements I concluded - and this is what you confirmed - that you took those photographs in 2002. But were you standing on the staircase when you took this first photograph, 68, the one in the upper left-hand corner, were you standing on the staircase when you took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, in my neighbour's yard on the staircase a little bit lower from the position from where I was observing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Further down or further up?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Lower. I was further up, but the photograph was taken from a position further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement you note that you were in the basement of your neighbour's house and that you looked through the window.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: This part here in the photograph on the second row is the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So this photograph that we looked at a little while ago was not taken from the location where you were on the 27th of March, 1999; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Which photograph are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go back to the photographs. So K002-3168.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I took this photograph from the staircase of my neighbour's yard but not from the position from where I was observing. The position I took the photograph from is a little bit lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Raka. Mr. Raka, in paragraph 14 of your statement, the one from 2006, in the second sentence it says: "The police officers lined up, got down on the ground, and started crawling around the factory." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Can you ask the question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me read a portion of your statement, that's paragraph 14, second sentence. "The police officers lined up, got down on the ground, and started crawling around the factory." And now I'm asking you is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Some of them were crawling, some of them were walking low, but some of them were definitely crawling.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Raka. Am I right when I say that you were not an eye-witness of the death of Halil Nikoci and Shefket Demi who were guards in the factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, I didn't, but I know that they were killed at the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the 2006 statement you say that you heard about it the next day from Halil's son. And in the statement that you gave in 1999 you say: "I know that their bodies were lying at the factory for a long time, and dogs ate them."

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I gave the statement after the war, and this was on the basis of the information I had, and the information that I had was that their bodies had been mauled by dogs, stray dogs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that you did not see, yourself, the killing of Jonuz, who you mention in paragraph 18?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, I didn't. However, I know that he was killed on the road close to my neighbour's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And tell me, you also did not see the killing of an old man whom you mention in paragraph 19?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I didn't. I only heard from his son that he had left his father at home killed by bullets. When we were going to Macedonia, I learned that information then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were not there in your house, in your yard, when your wife was wounded; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I was in the basement of my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And just one more thing, Mr. Raka. In your statement, the statement that you gave in 1999, there is no mention of what I'm about to read from paragraph 22 of your 2006 statement. "On the 28th of March, 1999, we saw people from the other end of Kacanik pass through our area. They told us that the police had taken away Sefedin Beqa's two sons and that Hamid Berisha had been killed. They told us that the police was going from house to house in the neighbourhood around Ramadan Agushi. Those people left their homes and were leaving town. My family and all our neighbours then decided to leave before the police came." So what I've just read to you is not contained anywhere in your 1999 statement; do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I only know that when people came towards our neighbourhood, they told us that the police had been expelling people. They told us also that Hamid Berisha had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
