utterances.text: Mr. Raka, I read out to you what is contained in your 2006 statement. Please listen to me carefully. There is no word of this quote in your 1999 statement, the one that you gave in November 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have it on the screen. So this is Defence document D002-6001.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said earlier, we made amendments to the 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But how could you change something that you didn't say?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Nothing was changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender the November 1999 statement made by this witness into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We haven't yet seen this document, and it hasn't been put to the witness. Are you wanting him to confirm that there is no reference in it to the subject matter of paragraph 22 of the statement in 2006? Is that the point? Perhaps he might be able to look at the earlier statement and confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, that's precisely what I'm trying to do. If I may assist you, it should be -- let me give you the exact reference in the statement -- yes, that's at page 4: "On the 28th of March." In English that would be this part of the statement, it's page 6: "On the 28th of March we started walking ..." And in Albanian that would be -- just a moment. It is easy to find it because it begins with a date -- well, here it is, yes, that's page 9 of the Albanian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, can you see this part where it says "Me 28th of March"? Would you please read it.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, do you agree that there is no mention of what I quoted a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Which things do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me clear this up to you. In this statement, the one that you gave in 1999, the paragraph begins with the words: "On 28th of March we started walking through the woods towards Macedonia ..." And in paragraph 22 you have all those things that I read out to you: "On the 28th of March, 1999, we saw people from the other end of Kacanik passing through the woods ..." and so on and so forth. So what I read out to you. And none of it is in your 1999 statement; do you agree with me when I say that?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The first sentence says it very clearly. My wife had to stay at home for two days, and it includes those other things that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Raka, please listen to what I'm saying. Your wife is not at issue here. I'm just saying that in your 1999 statement, what I read out to you does not contain the things that you said in 2006. And if you want me to quote to you again from paragraph 22 - but I don't think it's necessary - and to compare it to what you said in 1999.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I mentioned Sefedin's son's case because this is what people from the neighbourhood told us and that was the reason why we decided to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's what it says in paragraph 22 of your 2006 statement, and I'm now showing you your statement from 1999 where it says: "On the 28th of March we started walking through the woods towards Macedonia. We were in a large group ..." So all those things that are contained in paragraph 22 that I just read out to you are not contained in the part of your previous statement when you talk about your trip to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They were not included because the statement was shortened at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I please tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, I take it that you agree that you made this statement in 1999, the earlier statement, you made that statement, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00092, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Raka, just one more thing. My assistant has just drawn my attention to this. Is it true that this gentleman, Jonuz, was transferred from Kacanik to Pristina after he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know. According to the information from the person from the infirmary in Kacanik, they took him, but I only know that they took him to the infirmary building. After that I don't know, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Raka, for answering all my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions for Mr. Raka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Djurdjic. Ms. Nilsen, is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honours, no re-examination from Prosecution. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, we want to thank you very much for coming and being able to assist us with your recollection of these events. We now have your evidence that you've given today, and of course your two previous statements and the evidence that you gave when you came here last time. And we'll be studying that in due course. We thank you for being prepared to come and assist us again, and you now are free to return to your normal activities. The court officer will show you from the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Nilsen, do we understand that that concludes the witnesses that are available at the present time?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's correct. The Prosecution do not have any witness available for testifying today. That concludes the witnesses that we have scheduled for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So the replacement witnesses will be available to commence on Monday of next week?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And I gather there will now be four witnesses next week ?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I think it will, but I am not hundred per cent sure. I am looking at my colleague, Mr. Neuner, maybe he would be able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic seems to know more about your case than you do. He says there will be four.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I think it is correct. I think it is correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned friend Mr. Stamp informed us yesterday about the sequence of witnesses and the schedule for the following weeks and the Defence is fully apprised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, in that case we shall adjourn now to resume on Monday to continue with the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
